title: Title
notes: Open by naming the appendix as a comparison theorem factory rather than a grab bag of background. The source span starts by reviewing metric connections and torsion, then uses that machinery to compare the Chern connection on T^{1,0}X with the Levi-Civita connection on the underlying real tangent bundle. The later pages translate the same compatibility into holonomy language, with U(n) giving Kahler geometry and SU(n) adding a Ricci-flat consequence.

title: Two Connections
notes: This is the orientation slide. Students should see that the appendix compares not two unrelated gadgets, but two ways of transporting tangent vectors on the same manifold. The map u to one half of u minus i Iu identifies the real tangent bundle with the (1,0) tangent bundle. The question is whether the canonical complex connection and the canonical real connection line up under that identification.

title: Metric And Torsion
notes: The first technical move is to separate metric compatibility from torsion. Metric compatibility says the connection preserves inner products under transport. Torsion, by contrast, measures the skew part of covariant differentiation after the Lie bracket has removed the intrinsic noncommutativity of vector fields. In coordinates, the formula A(u)v minus A(v)u is the practical test: torsion is a real tensor, not an artifact of the chosen functions.

title: Levi-Civita
notes: The uniqueness statement is the anchor for the whole appendix. Once a connection is both metric and torsion-free, there is no further freedom left. That is why a Hermitian connection cannot usually become Levi-Civita merely by forgetting complex structure: there are many Hermitian connections. The later propositions succeed only when the induced real connection also lands inside this tiny intersection.

title: Torsion-Free Forms
notes: This result explains why torsion-free is more than a formal condition. In the torsion-free case, the covariant derivative formula for d has no extra correction terms. The important downstream use is for the fundamental two-form omega. Once a connection is metric and commutes with the complex structure, omega is parallel. Torsion-free then promotes parallelness to closedness, which is the Kahler condition.

title: Hermitian Structure
notes: Now the real tangent bundle is given complex structure. A Hermitian metric is not an extra metric floating above the Riemannian one; it is the same real metric made compatible with I. The fundamental form omega packages the metric and I together. The map Phi is the practical bridge: it turns a real tangent vector into its (1,0) component, so a connection on T^{1,0}X can be read as a real connection when appropriate.

title: Hermitian To Metric
notes: This lemma is deliberately modest. If a connection preserves the Hermitian metric on the complex tangent bundle, then its real part preserves the Riemannian metric. This explains why the Chern connection is a plausible candidate for comparison with Levi-Civita. However, Levi-Civita uniqueness has two hypotheses. The bridge lemma supplies metricity, but the torsion calculation has to do the remaining work.

title: Torsion-Free Hermitian
notes: This proposition is the first major bridge theorem. The proof has a local calculation hidden inside it: zero torsion forces the connection form to have the type condition expected of the Chern connection. Once the induced real connection is metric and torsion-free, Levi-Civita uniqueness applies. Finally, since the connection preserves both g and I, it preserves omega, and the torsion-free exterior derivative formula makes omega closed.

title: Kahler Equivalence
notes: This is the summary theorem the lecturer should pause on. The source span phrases the conclusion as four equivalent conditions: Levi-Civita makes I parallel, the metric is Kahler, Levi-Civita and Chern are identified by the tangent isomorphism, and the Chern connection is torsion-free. The point is not memorizing a chain of implications; it is recognizing the same compatibility appearing as a differential form condition, a connection condition, and a torsion condition.

title: Curvature
notes: After the Kahler equivalence, the appendix turns to curvature. The Riemannian curvature formula is the commutator of covariant derivatives corrected by the derivative along the Lie bracket. For a tangent bundle connection, this is exactly the usual bundle curvature. This matters because the later Ricci formula can be read either through Riemannian curvature tensors or through the Chern curvature of T^{1,0}X.

title: Ricci
notes: The Ricci comparison is where the two languages become computationally interchangeable. The Riemannian Ricci tensor is converted to a real two-form by inserting I in the first slot. On a Kahler manifold, the curvature of the common tangent connection is of type (1,1), and the Ricci form can be obtained either by contracting with the Kahler form or by taking the complex trace of the endomorphism-valued curvature.

title: Parallel Transport
notes: Parallel transport is the mechanism by which a connection becomes group-theoretic. Pull the tangent bundle back to the interval, solve the flat-section equation, and the initial vector determines a final vector. Metric compatibility says lengths and inner products do not change. When the path closes, the resulting operators form the holonomy group, a subgroup of the orthogonal group at the base point.

title: Berger Snapshot
notes: The appendix invokes Berger's theorem only as a snapshot, not as a proof target. Under standard hypotheses such as simply connected, irreducible, and not locally symmetric, the possible holonomy groups are highly restricted. For this course, the important entries are U(n) and SU(n), with Sp(n) nearby because of hyperkahler geometry. The classification tells us that holonomy reduction is a major geometric event, not a cosmetic change of notation.

title: Holonomy Principle
notes: The holonomy principle is the conceptual payoff. If a tensor at one tangent space is fixed by all closed-loop transports, then parallel transport defines the same tensor everywhere with no path ambiguity. For a U(n) holonomy reduction, the invariant tensor is an almost complex structure I_x. Its parallel extension has I squared equal to minus the identity everywhere, and the torsion-free connection ensures the resulting complex structure is integrable, so the metric is Kahler.

title: U(n) And SU(n)
notes: This final mathematical slide states the two propositions at the end of the appendix in teaching form. U(n) holonomy gives an invariant complex structure, hence a parallel complex structure and a Kahler metric. SU(n) holonomy strengthens the invariant data: the determinant representation is trivial, so a parallel holomorphic volume form appears. Combined with the Ricci formula for the canonical bundle, this yields Ricci-flatness.
